Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Ms. Neetu Singh, Advocate for the

Heard.
Admit.
Mr. Rajesh Sharma, Advocate, takes 
notice for the respondent no.1.
Ms. Prabha Naithani and Mr. Gaurav 
Pawar, Advocates take notice for the 
respondent nos. 2 to 5.
Issue notice to the respondent no.6 
returnable within four weeks.
Steps to be taken within a week.
List this matter on 12.10.2023.
Heard on Interim Relief Application IA 
No.1 of 2023.
It is the case of the petitioners that 
after the death of their father, the family 
pension has not been shared with them and 
the second wife of the father has been 
granted the entire family pension in 
defiance to the regulation 40 of the Union 
Bank of India (Employees) Pension 
Regulations, 1995, which has been quoted 
in Para 17 of the writ petition. The relevant 
portion reads as follows:-
Where the deceased employee or  pensioner is survived by a widow but 
has left behind eligible child or 
children from another wife who is not 
alive, the eligible child or children 
shall be entitled to the share of 
family pension which the mother 
would have received if she had been 
alive at the time of the death of the 
employee pensioner:
Having considered, as an interim 
measure, till the next date of listing, no 
further family pension shall be paid to the 
respondent no.6
Interim relief application stands 
disposed of, accordingly. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
04.07.2023

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 934 of 2023
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Ms. Neetu Singh and Mr. Vinod Joshi, 
Advocates for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India /respondent no. 1.
3. Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, Advocate for 
the respondent nos. 2 to 5.
4. Ms. Ranjana Kumari and Mr. Kanti Ram 
Sharma, Advocate for respondent no. 6.
5. One Mr. Bikram Pal retired from the post 
of Deputy Branch Manager from Union Bank of 
India on 31.12.2018 and thereafter he died on 
13.11.2021. Mr. Bikram Pal had married twice, 
initially with one Ms. Savita and after her death 
on 30.04.2004, he re-married with one Ms.
Kurmala (respondent no. 6) on 08.05.2005. 
The entire dues, including family pension was 
paid to the second wife (respondent no. 6). 
6. This writ petition is filed by the children 
born out from the first wife, challenging the 
pension payment order in favour of respondent 
no. 6, on 01.01.2019.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner 
contends that the eldest daughter of the 
deceased employee Ms. Anjali Katariya suffers 
from Schizophrenia, therefore, as per the  applicable Rules, she is also entitled to family 
pension. 
8. Learned counsel for the bank however, 
submits that in the absence of any certificate 
issued by a competent authority, the assertion 
made on behalf of the petitioner that Ms. Anjali 
Katariya is suffering from Schizophrenia,
cannot be accepted. 
9. Learned counsel for the petitioner 
submitted that a Medical Board headed by 
Chief Medical Officer, Haridwar has certified 
that Ms. Anjali Katariya suffers from
Schizophrenia. 
10. Learned counsel for the bank, however, 
submits that as per the Rules applicable in the 
bank, the disability/ailment has to be examined 
by a doctor empanelled/approved by the bank 
and such certificate alone can be considered. 
11. Court had directed learned counsel for the 
bank to get instructions regarding the doctor, 
who is approved by the bank. Today, on 
instructions, he submits that one Dr. Kapil 
Arora, whose particulars are given below, has 
been approved by the bank: 
Dr. Kapil Arora,
H.No. 56/57, Madhubani, 
Uttarigaon, Near Kasiga School, 
Dehradun-248009
Ph. No. 7351300900
 7451900300. 
12. Therefore, Ms. Anjali Katariya can be 
produced before the said doctor for  examination and if the said doctor certifies that 
she suffers from some disability, then bank will 
do the needful as per the Rules. 
13. In such view of the matter, let 
Ms. Anjali Katariya be examined by 
Dr. Kapil Arora, on 17.11.2025. The doctor 
concerned shall submit his report, including 
certificate, if any, in the office of Regional 
Manager, Union Bank of India, situate at 
Dehradun. The Regional Manager concerned 
shall ensure that all the documents submitted 
by the concerned doctor are transmitted to the 
counsel appearing for the bank within one 
week thereafter.
14. List on 10.12.2025.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 12.11.2025
Navin

Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Ms. Neetu Singh with Mr. Vinod Joshi, learned 
Counsel for the petitioner.
2. None is present for respondent no.1.
3. Mr. V.K. Guglani, learned Counsel for 
respondent nos.2 to 5.
4. Ms. Ranjana Kumari appearing through V.C. 
with Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, learned Counsel for 
respondent no.6.
5. Vide order dated 12.11.2025, this Court had 
directed petitioner no.1 (Anjali Katariya) to be 
medically examined by Dr. Kapil Arora on 17.11.2025 
regarding the disease suffered by her i.e. 
Schizophrenia.
6. Today, learned Counsel appearing for respondent 
–Bank submits that petitioner no.1 could not be 
examined as Dr. Kapil Arora showed his reluctance to 
examine petitioner no.1 since he is a mere physician 
and was not an expert Psychiatrist. 
7. In such view of the matter, in order to get 
petitioner no.1 (Anjali Katariya) medically examined, 
this Court is of the view that she must be examined by 
a panel of doctors one of whom must be a 
Psychiatrist.  8. Accordingly, the Chief Medical Officer (CMO), 
Haridwar is directed to constitute a Medical Board of 
three doctors within one week from today; the Medical 
Board must be consisting of one Neurologist, one 
Psychiatrist and one other doctor of his choice; the 
C.M.O. Haridwar shall fix the date and time for 
examination of petitioner no.1 (Anjali Katariya) and 
inform petitioner nos.2 to 4 for the same; the Medical 
Board shall examine petitioner no.1; and submit its 
report to this Court straightway.
9. List this matter on 05.08.2026 along with the 
report.
10. Registry to send a copy of this order, along with 
complete memo of parties and their addresses, today 
itself, to the C.M.O. Haridwar for information and 
compliance.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 20.07.2026 R.Dang

Anjali Katariya & others

 Versus

Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Ms. Neetu Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioner (appeared through V.C.).
2. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, learned counsel for 
respondent no.1 (appeared through V.C.).
3. Mr. B.S. Koranga, learned counsel holding brief 
of Mr. V.K. Guglani, learned counsel for respondent 
nos.2 to 5.
4. Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, learned counsel for 
respondent no.6.
5. This Court, vide order dated 20.07.2026, 
directed the Chief Medical Officer, Haridwar, to 
constitute a Medical Board of three doctors within 
one week from the date of the order. The Medical 
Board was directed to consist of one Neurologist, one 
Psychiatrist, and one other doctor of his choice, 
fixing the date and time for the examination of 
petitioner no.1 (Anjali Katariya) and informing 
petitioner nos. 2 to 4 of the same. The Medical Board 
was directed to examine petitioner no.1 and submit a 
report straightaway, fixing the case on 05.08.2026.
6. Today, the matter was called. There is a letter of 
the CMO, Haridwar, dated 30.07.2026, addressed to  the Deputy Registrar (Judicial), whereby the CMO, 
Haridwar, has informed that in District Haridwar, 
there was no Neurologist posted, therefore, petitioner 
no.1 cannot be examined as per the order passed by 
this Court dated 20.07.2026. He advised in his letter 
that petitioner no.1 (Anjali Katariya) be medically 
examined either at Doon Medical College, Dehradun, 
or AIIMS, Rishikesh.
7. Having taken cognizance of this letter, this 
Court directs the Director, AIIMS, Rishikesh, to 
constitute a Medical Board of three members within 
one week from today, consisting of one Neurologist, 
one Psychiatrist, and one other doctor of the choice 
of the Director. The Medical Board, so constituted, 
shall fix the date and time for the examination of 
petitioner no.1 (Anjali Katariya) and inform petitioner 
nos.2 to 4 of the same. The Medical Board shall 
examine petitioner no.1 and submit the report to this 
Court straightaway.
8. List on 16.09.2026.
9. Registry is directed to send the copy of order to 
the Director, AIIMS, Rishikesh within 24 hours. 
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
18.08.2026 AK
